content.title: RULES EVERY NEW PARENT NEEDS BEFORE THE {{FIRST}} MONTH ENDS
facts: **Eat standing up if you have to** – a rushed meal with real food still beats skipping it, protein and fiber keep your energy steadier than coffee alone.
**Nap when the baby naps once a day, not every time** – use at least one nap window for a 20-minute lie-down, chronic sleep debt hits your immune system fast.
**Batch one meal on Sundays** – cook a double portion of anything and freeze half, so exhausted-you at 9pm has an actual option besides cereal.
**Keep a water bottle in every room you feed in** – breastfeeding and bottle-feeding both spike thirst, and dehydration makes fatigue feel worse than it is.
**Ask for a 2-hour block off, not a full day** – short, specific breaks are easier for partners/family to actually deliver, and they still lower stress hormones.
**Get outside for 10 minutes even in pajamas** – daylight exposure early on helps reset your own sleep rhythm, which is already disrupted enough.
**Lower your shower standard to 5 minutes** – a quick shower daily protects your mood more than people admit, don't wait for a 'free' 20 minutes that won't come.
**Say no to visitors in the first 2 weeks if you're depleted** – recovery time matters more than politeness, your body is still healing.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.
content.caption:
New parents burn through nutrients and sleep faster than almost anyone realizes, so a few small fixes matter more than they sound. Water intake drops off fast when you're feeding a baby every few hours, and even mild dehydration mimics exhaustion — your body pulls fluid from everywhere else first, brain included, which is part of why the fog feels so heavy. Daylight in the first 10 minutes outside isn't just a mood trick either — it helps reset your circadian rhythm, which gets scrambled hard by nighttime feeds, so your body has an easier time knowing when to actually feel sleepy later. And that 2-hour block off isn't just rest for rest's sake — short recovery windows lower cortisol enough to measurably improve patience and focus for hours afterward. Every parent's capacity looks different, so adjust to what your days actually allow.
